title: Ambrosian book states: bounded calendar and prayer revisions

traditions.label: Ambrosian Missal
traditions.scope: Historical and reformed Latin source states of Milan; independent translation history deferred.
traditions.coverage_note: Selective, non-exhaustive; dates attest manuscript evidence, publication, approval or effectiveness, never continuous validity. 1913 critical publication, 1990 Italian updated reprint and 2026 Latin publication are not counted as extra reforms. Documented means the stated evidence supports the bounded claim, not a checked native-text transcription. Separate Italian translation history is deferred.

sources.title: BnF FRBNF 36814098: Missale ambrosianum duplex

sources.limitations: Catalogue establishes the critical edition, not any individual textual delta.

sources.title: Ratti and Magistretti, Missale ambrosianum duplex (1913)
sources.inspection: Gallica item, complete PDF, texteBrut, IIIF and services resolver requests returned 403 in this environment; IA title search found no institutional copy of this critical edition.

sources.title: Jacopo Maria Calloni, La tradizione manoscritta del messale ambrosiano
sources.inspection: Read rendered title page and p. 142: 1751 / 1902 comparison, Ceriani revision project, 1877 permission and manuscript consultation. Screenshot failed.
sources.limitations: Doctoral research; historical overview is not direct inspection of 1751 / 1902 books or the 1877 act. Quoted dates and general account remain source-described.

sources.title: Uwe Michael Lang, Votive Masses of the Holy Face of Christ in Early Printed Diocesan Missals, Mediaeval Studies 79 (2017), 165–203
sources.inspection: Complete publisher PDF acquired. Page 169/PDF 5, including notes 12–13, visually inspected against its page image on 2026-10-17.
sources.limitations: Original comparative research. Its 1475 Veronica attestation is additionally checked in Vatican images; its 1594 removal remains scholarly description because the 1594 original was not inspected. The suggested reason for removal is explicitly probable.

sources.title: Anthony Ward, Modern Ambrosian Prefaces of Saints: Points of Contact with the Roman Missal, Notitiae 32 (1996), 238–267
sources.inspection: Complete official issue acquired, SHA256 ad5dc11915d96ea271fa6da34923ac128a2c4d72f47aec8f469399a707479aca. Article pp 241–244/PDF 63–66 and 266–267/PDF 88–89 visually inspected, including quoted Latin and edition-specific footnotes.
sources.limitations: Image-checking Ward verifies what his article says; it does not independently collate the 1902, 1954 or 1981 altar books. Source-described changes only. Publication in an official journal does not turn scholarship into legislation.

sources.limitations: Complete decree also image-checked in official 2024 frontmatter, printed IX/PDF 9. Attached approved exemplar remains unavailable; general revision description does not date each prayer change.

sources.title: Mario Delpini, complete decree promulgating the second Ambrosian Missal, 28 March 2024

stages.label: Early printed Sanctoral
stages.scope: Selected Sanctoral attestation; not a reconstruction of the entire book.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan, Antonio Zarotto, 1475; British Library IB. 25954; compare Vatican Inc. III. 420.
stages.summary: February 4 Veronica feast and Mass attested.

evidence.claim: Identifies the early printed formulary.
Original images directly attest the Veronica proper, Gospel sequence and ending before the Agatha proper.

stages.limitations: Direct original-page reading establishes the bounded proper. Calendar date remains scholarly-described; 1594 removal has not been independently checked. 1499 corroborates this item, not whole-book identity.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Post-Tridentine Sanctoral
stages.scope: Veronica removal only; other revision contents remain unexamined.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan, 1594; British Library Legg 137, described by Lang as Pacifico Da Ponte.
stages.summary: Veronica feast removed in the cited witness.

evidence.claim: Names the 1594 comparator for removal.

stages.limitations: Printer differs from Sabbio-labelled catalogue leads; use exact shelfmark and resolve before acquisition. No claim 1594 was the first effective removal. The 1981 Institutio n. 7 states, as an official retrospective, that the 1594 Missal is not far from the 1475 printing while taking some items from Pius V's Missal; it does not list them. The 1640 edition, directly inspected, lacks the Veronica proper, which is consistent with but does not verify the 1594 removal.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Monti's revised Milan missal
stages.scope: Archiepiscopal edition whose prefatory letter states its revision programme; calendar of February and the Sanctoral around 3-5 February checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan: Giovanni Ambrogio Sirturi with the heirs of Pontio and Piccaglia, archiepiscopal printers, 1640; letter of Cardinal Cesare Monti
stages.summary: Monti's letter says a new edition was needed, that ancient manuscripts, liturgical writers and Milanese records were consulted, that proper prayers and whole Masses of certain saints, instituted after the last edition or by Monti himself, were put in their places, and that the chant notation was restored on expert advice. The 4 February calendar entry is the Chair of Peter at Antioch; the Sanctoral passes from Blaise to that Chair (by referral) and then to Agatha, with no Veronica Mass.

evidence.claim: Identifies the Milan 1640 archiepiscopal printing.
States consultation of old manuscripts, insertion of saints' prayers and Masses instituted since the last edition, and restoration of chant notation.

evidence.locus: February calendar PDF 11; Sanctoral printed p. 396, PDF 434; index PDF 9
evidence.claim: 4 February is the Chair of Peter at Antioch; no Veronica proper stands between Blaise and Agatha, and the saints index has no Veronica entry.

stages.limitations: The letter names the kinds of change but not each changed formulary, and does not name the edition it revises. The absence of a Veronica proper is bounded to the inspected calendar, index and Sanctoral page; it does not date the removal, which Lang reports already for 1594. No whole-book collation.
stages.reception: The letter commends the book to the priests of the Milanese Church. Continuous or exclusive use is not established.

stages.label: Pozzobonelli Temporal
stages.scope: Proprium de tempore represented in the 1913 parallel critical edition.
stages.summary: Identified older Temporal state awaiting direct comparison.

evidence.claim: Names 1751 / 1902 comparanda.
Explains the paired critical edition.

stages.limitations: Not a transcription; original 1751 title page and liturgical approval unread.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Ceriani–Ferrari revised missal
stages.scope: Identified typical edition; Temporal and selected Sanctoral preface evidence.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, editio typica, Milan, Agnelli, 1902; Ferrari authority.
stages.summary: Revised state associated with Ceriani manuscript research.

evidence.claim: Describes revision using older manuscripts.
Identifies 1902 pp. 401–402.

stages.limitations: Full book not read. 1751 → 1902 textual deltas remain uncollated. No 1974 predecessor identity inferred from chronological adjacency.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Schuster's fifth printing after the 1902 typical
stages.scope: Conformed printing of the 1902 typical edition with an approved appendix of Masses for some congregations; three Sanctoral prefaces checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, editio quinta post typicam, Milan: Daverio, 1954
stages.summary: Schuster's decree reports that the censor certified agreement with the 1902 typical edition and approves an appendix of Masses for some congregations adapted to the Ambrosian rite. The Sebastian preface begins Aeterne Deus. Quoniam beati Martyris tui Sebastiani; the Nativity of John preface begins Aeterne Deus: Et in die festivitatis hodiernae and reads conceptus abstersit; the Decollation preface begins Aequum et salutare and narrates the beheading.

evidence.claim: Fifth printing after the typical edition; censor certifies agreement with the 1902 typical; appendix approved; dated 21 March 1954.
Directly read Sebastian, Nativity of John and Decollation prefaces.

stages.limitations: A conformed printing, not a new recension; it stands for the 1902 typical text only as far as the censor's certificate reaches. The appendix contents were not inspected. Selected pages only.
stages.reception: Approved by the archbishop for publication for the Ambrosian rite; use in particular churches is not established.

stages.label: Approved postconciliar source
stages.scope: Reformed Latin texts approved 30 November 1974; attached exemplar unavailable.
stages.summary: Reform includes Roman-source and newly composed prayers.

evidence.claim: Approves reformed Latin source and describes enrichment.

stages.limitations: Approval is not a 1974 printed book or proof of word-for-word identity with 1981.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Approved special Eucharistic prayers
stages.scope: Latin Ambrosian Eucharistic prayers for Holy Thursday and the Easter Vigil, separately confirmed after the general 1974 approval.
stages.witness_label: Prot. CD191/75, official confirmation entry Notitiae 11 (1975), 346.
stages.summary: A distinct component approval, not evidence of a second whole-missal reform.

evidence.claim: Names the two occasions, Latin language and 1 September 1975 confirmation.

stages.limitations: Prayer texts and attached exemplars not printed in the entry; exact relation to 1981 publication is not text-collated.
stages.reception: Approved Ambrosian use for the two named celebrations; no universal Roman or continuous-unchanged-use claim.

stages.label: Colombo's promulgation of the reformed missal
stages.scope: Archiepiscopal promulgation of the reformed Missale Ambrosianum and its Institutio, as reprinted in the 1981 Latin book; no separate 1976 Latin volume inspected.
stages.witness_label: Decree of Giovanni Colombo, Milan, Palm Sunday 11 April 1976, printed V-VII in the 1981 Missale Ambrosianum
stages.summary: Colombo promulgates the new Missal, describes abandoned or changed older prayers, new compositions, enriched formularies and two restored or expanded anaphoras for the Holy Thursday and Easter Vigil Masses, and makes the Missal and its Institutio obligatory in all Ambrosian-rite churches and parishes of the diocese from 14 November 1976, the first Sunday of Advent.

evidence.claim: Dateline 11 April 1976; obligatory use from 14 November 1976; names the two anaphoras and the kinds of revision.

stages.limitations: The decree is read in its 1981 reprint. Its effective date is a prescription, not proof of uniform implementation. It does not identify which Latin volume, if any, was printed in 1976; the 1976 Italian book remains a deferred translation witness.
stages.reception: Prescribed for all churches and parishes of the Ambrosian rite in the Archdiocese of Milan; actual compliance is not established.

stages.label: First postconciliar Latin book
stages.scope: Published Latin source: front matter, the two special Eucharistic prayers and selected Sanctoral prefaces directly read in an acquired scan; calendar organization represented only through the official Latin publisher's retrospective account, not a reconstructed calendar.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Mediolani 1981, promulgated under Giovanni Colombo; Ward MA.
stages.summary: Printed first-reform witness. It reprints Colombo's 1976 promulgation and the 1974 confirmation, and adds Martini's 8 September 1981 promulgation of changes to rite or texts introduced since 1976 with Apostolic See confirmation. Prex eucharistica V is prescribed for the Holy Thursday evening Mass and VI for the Easter Vigil.

evidence.claim: Identifies 1981 publication and prior 1974 approval.
Identifies 1981 as preceding Latin edition.

evidence.locus: Description: paragraph beginning La pubblicazione della II edizione latina and following principal-changes list, especially La riorganizzazione dell’anno liturgico
evidence.claim: Identifies the first Latin edition of 1981 as the book replaced and describes the successor’s reorganization into seasons after Epiphany and Pentecost. This supplies a retrospective predecessor-calendar scope, without individual 1981 assignments.

evidence.locus: Title PDF 7; printed V-VII, PDF 9-11; Prot. 2347/74, PDF 12
evidence.claim: Mediolani MCMLXXXI title; Colombo 1976 decree; Martini 1981 note promulgating post-1976 confirmed changes in this edition; 1974 confirmation reprinted.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 527 and 535, PDF 611 and 619, MA 213 and 214 (opening rubrics)
evidence.claim: Prex eucharistica V for the Holy Thursday evening Mass and VI for the Easter Vigil, matching the occasions confirmed in 1975.
Directly read reformed Sebastian, Nativity of John and Passion of John prefaces and the Common of Martyrs collect.

stages.limitations: A complete scan is acquired for research only; selected pages are read and nothing is transcribed. 1974 approved exemplar and 1975 confirmations are not collated with this book: the matching occasions of Prex V and VI do not prove word-for-word identity with the 1975 exemplars. Martini's note says post-1976 changes exist without listing them; no separate 1981 reform is asserted. This publication and the 1974 approval must not be counted as two independently established substantive recensions. Calendar evidence is retrospective and structural only: no 1981 calendar page, feast assignment or Sunday count has been inspected. The evidence does not transfer the Italian 1976/1990 calendar's exact contents into the Latin 1981 book.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Second reformed source recension
stages.scope: Second Latin typical source and Italian expression; effective 17 November 2024.
stages.witness_label: Latin second typical text approved 7 December 2023; Italian 2024 ISBN 9788868946821; Latin 2026 ISBN 9788868948627.
stages.summary: Reorganized year, updated saints and expanded prayer repertory.

evidence.claim: Approves Latin source and Italian translation.
Promulgates both texts; effective 17 November 2024.
Associates 2026 Latin publication with second recension.
Separates 1976 first Italian edition, 1986 update, 1990 updated reprint, 2024 second edition; establishes full 2023 approval and 28 March 2024 promulgation with 17 November 2024 effect.

stages.limitations: Complete offered front matter is inspected, but whole 2024 book and 2026 Latin edition are not collated. 1990 is expressly an updated Italian reprint. 2023 approval, 2024 effectiveness and 2026 Latin publication are distinct events of the second recension; no separate reform is inferred from each. Latin loci for the named new propers remain unverified.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

transitions.summary: Veronica feast and proper Mass disappear.

changes.locus_after: 1594 British Library Legg 137; exact page not supplied

evidence.claim: Comparative description of removal.
Reports feast excision.

transitions.limitations: Source-described, not independent negative search or collation. Intervening editions unreviewed; not an immediate-successor edge. Proposed motivation remains Lang’s probable explanation.

transitions.summary: Between the two inspected printings the Veronica proper that precedes Agatha in 1475 is no longer present in the 1640 Sanctoral, calendar or saints index.

changes.before: In sancte veronice proper begins f. 35r, Gospel Mark 5:21, and ends f. 36r before In sancte agathe.
changes.after: After Blaise, the Sanctoral gives the Chair of Peter at Antioch by referral and then Agatha; no Veronica proper; the 4 February calendar entry is the Antioch Chair and the index has no Veronica.
changes.locus_before: 1475 Vatican Inc. III. 420, ff. 35r-36r, IIIF canvases 76-78
changes.locus_after: 1640 printed p. 396 (PDF 434); calendar PDF 11; index PDF 9

evidence.claim: Veronica proper directly read before Agatha.
No Veronica proper, calendar entry or index entry in the inspected places.
Before state directly inspected.
After state directly inspected.

transitions.limitations: Original-to-original comparison of one proper across 165 years and unseen intervening editions (1594, 1609 and others); it neither dates the removal nor makes 1640 the first book without it. Lang's 1594 report and the 1475 calendar date remain scholarly. Not an immediate-successor edge.

transitions.summary: Older readings were sought through manuscript comparison; exact changed units remain unidentified here.

evidence.claim: Reports Ceriani restoration project and 1913 synopsis.
Identifies the paired Temporal.

transitions.limitations: Revision project established, but dossier lacks a checked before/after unit. Do not count this proposal as a demonstrated unit-level transition. 1877 permission is not a complete textual stage; 1913 is not a reform.

transitions.summary: The 1954 printing is certified by the archdiocesan censor to agree with the 1902 typical edition and adds an approved appendix of Masses for certain religious congregations, adapted to the Ambrosian rite by authority of the Apostolic See.

evidence.claim: Fifth printing after the typical; censor certifies full agreement with the 1902 typical edition; appendix approved.

transitions.limitations: Certified conformity, not an independent collation of the 1902 book; the appendix is a component addition whose contents were not inspected.

transitions.summary: Selected Sanctoral prefaces were replaced, shortened or reordered; related older material also survives in a different genre.

changes.before: Prenatal joy, parental healing and prophetic witness precede naming and sanctification.
changes.after: Moves naming and sanctification first; omits parental-healing clauses.

evidence.claim: Displays predecessor and successor; describes abbreviation and reordering.

changes.before: The older Ambrosian Passion-of-John feast had its own preface.
changes.after: The reformed Passion-of-John preface draws on the modern Roman John-the-Baptist preface, with adaptations and Ambrosian conclusion.
changes.locus_before: Older preface described by Ward pp 241–242
changes.locus_after: 1981 MA 384/6, printed p. 717 (Ward p. 240 prints MA84/6; in the 1981 book MA 84 is a Lenten feria); Ward p. 242

evidence.claim: Describes replacement by the modern Roman-source preface; article pages image-inspected.

changes.before: Sebastian proper used the preface printed 1902 p 330 and 1954 p 465.
changes.after: The Sebastian preface is replaced at 1981 MA 248/6. Related older material, mediated by the modern Roman Common-of-Martyrs preface, appears as an Ambrosian Common-of-Martyrs collect MA483/2; it is not the new Sebastian preface.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes replacement of the Sebastian preface from reuse as a collect elsewhere, and identifies the immediate modern Roman source.
Notes 1902/1954 variant; not exact identity.

transitions.limitations: Three selected preface findings described by Ward; no complete-book inheritance or immediate 1902 → 1981 succession. Dates of first introduction within the postconciliar reform remain unresolved. Article page images were checked on 2026-10-17; the underlying old and new altar books have not been independently collated. Ward p 243 n 12 distinguishes 1902 abstersit from a 1954 abstulit, but the 1954 original page (p. 572) reads abstersit (and quo, not qua), so the supposed 1902/1954 variant is not supported by the inspected 1954 book; Ward's 1954 quotation is not a diplomatic transcription. The Passion-of-John and Sebastian findings remain scholarly-described, including the distinction between replacement of a preface and reuse of related material as a collect. The three findings are now also checked original-to-original from 1954 to 1981 in ambrosian-1954-to-1981-prefaces.

transitions.summary: Page-level comparison of the 1954 printing and the 1981 reformed book confirms replacement of the Sebastian and Passion-of-John prefaces and recasting of the Nativity-of-John preface.

changes.before: Sebastian preface: Aeterne Deus. Quoniam beati Martyris tui Sebastiani pro confessione nominis tui venerabilis sanguis effusus, with the clauses mirabilia manifestat and perficis in infirmitate virtutem.
changes.after: Sebastian preface MA 248/6 is a different text: Qui suam in nos dilectionem manifestavit in finem, naming Sebastian as a true disciple who gave the supreme testimony of love.

evidence.claim: Old Sebastian preface directly read.
Replacement Sebastian preface directly read.

changes.before: Decollation of John preface: Aequum et salutare ... In quo beatus Joannes Baptista martyrii est coronam adeptus, narrating the beheading for forbidding an unlawful marriage and his announcing Christ's descent to the dead.
changes.after: Passion of John preface MA 384/6: In cuius praecursore beato Ioanne tuam magnificentiam collaudamus, with the baptism of Christ and the supreme testimony of his blood.

evidence.claim: Old Decollation preface directly read.
Replacement preface directly read; agrees with Ward's displayed text.

changes.before: Nativity of John in die: Et in die festivitatis hodiernae, quo beatus Baptista Joannes exortus est, exultare; prenatal leap, conceptus abstersit and the father's loosed tongue precede the naming and filling with the Spirit.
changes.after: MA 329/6: Et te in hodiernae die festivitatis excolere; naming and filling with the Spirit come first, the parental-healing clauses are absent, and a new conclusion follows.

evidence.claim: Old preface directly read, including abstersit.
Recast preface directly read.
Before states directly read.

evidence.locus: MA 248/6, 329/6, 384/6 (MA 483/2 for the recurrence in limitations)
evidence.claim: After states directly read.

transitions.limitations: Four bounded units, read on page images and not transcribed; no complete-book diff. 1954 is a conformed printing of the 1902 typical, so the change is not dated to 1954-1981 more narrowly than the 1974 approval and 1976 promulgation allow. Shared wording between the old preface and the 1981 collect does not by itself establish the route of borrowing; the Roman mediation is Ward's attribution. The Roman 1970 sources were not checked here. The old Sebastian preface's clauses sanguis effusus, mirabilia manifestat and perficis in infirmitate virtutem recur, recast, in the Common of Martyrs super populum MA 483/2 (1981 p. 832, PDF 916, directly read). Ward (pp. 266–267, nn. 71–73) attributes this to mediation through the modern Roman Common-of-Martyrs preface; because shared wording does not establish the route, the recurrence is recorded as an observation, not as a before/after change of this transition.

transitions.summary: Publication witnesses the approved reform; exact intervening changes unresolved.

evidence.claim: Links earlier approval with 1981 Latin publication.

transitions.limitations: No new substantive 1981 revision claimed and no exact identity certified. 1975 Eucharistic-prayer confirmation needs separate examination.

transitions.summary: The 1981 Latin edition reprints the 1976 promulgation and, by Martini's note, also promulgates changes to rite or texts introduced since 1976 with Apostolic See confirmation.

evidence.claim: Martini's note of 8 September 1981 promulgates in this edition the confirmed post-1976 changes.

transitions.limitations: The note does not list the changes, so no concrete before/after unit is asserted; the edge records the stated relationship only.

transitions.summary: Liturgical-year organization and prayer repertory revised.

Latin successor replaces 1981 and receives structural/repertory changes.
Promulgates substantive second recension.

Full decree names calendar/lectionary 20 March 2008, saints calendar 27 March 2010, saints lectionary 1 April 2010 and Vigil book 29 June 2015 as intervening changes incorporated in the second missal.

transitions.limitations: Full 2023 confirmation and 2024 promulgation now checked; exact before/after Latin prayer units remain uncollated. The decree explicitly retrospectively identifies 2008, 2010 and 2015 component changes: they are not asserted to be separate whole-missal editions. 2020 Italian translation changes are not independent Latin source revisions. Sunday-count discrepancy 32 (decree) versus 34 (publisher) remains explicit.

gaps.missing: Actual 1913 parallel pages and apparatus; exact original editions and substantive departures.
gaps.next_source: BnF cb 368140989; Gallica bpt 6 k 15031331; entire XXIV + 475-page critical edition, then original 1751 / 1902 witnesses. Gallica access was refused again on 2026-10-21 (HTTP 403 for site pages) and archive.org was unreachable; the 1981 Institutio n. 8 only states that the 1609 and 1902 editions reproduced older exemplars more faithfully.
gaps.consequence: 1751 / 1902 remain identified states with only provisional transition; no fictitious 1913 stage.

gaps.missing: The 1594 original itself (Veronica removal, imprint discrepancy and Pius V borrowings) and the 1609 Borromeo edition named by the 1981 Institutio; concrete formulary changes between 1594, 1609, 1640, 1712 and 1751. The 1640 Monti edition is now a documented stage and lacks the Veronica proper; the 1712 Archinto edition's letter describes an emended reprint of the latest exemplar, not a stated revision.
gaps.next_source: BL Legg 137; Alessandrina Y g 5 (Usuarium 6041); BnF 1594 Sabbio record; any 1609 Federico Borromeo printing; then compare named formularies across 1594, 1640 (PDF 434 and following) and 1712. MDZ and web searches on 2026-10-21 found no digitized 1594 or 1609 copy; archive.org and Gallica were unreachable or refused.
gaps.consequence: The removal is bounded between 1499 (Lang) and the directly inspected 1640 book, with Lang's 1594 report still scholarly; no complete 1475 to 1751 chain.

gaps.missing: Intervening 1902-1954 rubrical supplements, the 1974 approved exemplar, the 1975 confirmed prayer exemplars and the specific post-1976 changes that Martini's 1981 note promulgates without listing. The 1954 book, the 1981 front matter (Colombo 1976 decree with 14 November 1976 obligation, Martini 1981 note, 1974 confirmation) and the 1981 Prex V and VI are now directly inspected.
gaps.next_source: Any separately printed 1976 Latin Missal or fascicles; Notitiae 1976-1981 confirmation entries for post-1976 Ambrosian changes; Ward 1996 n. 5; collation of 1981 Prex V-VI against any published 1975 exemplar.
gaps.consequence: Approval (1974), prescription (1976) and publication (1981) are now separate dated events; individual alterations are still not dated to one of them.

gaps.missing: Exact Latin before/after units and original 2008/2010/2015 component books. Full 2023 decree, 2024 frontmatter and promulgation are acquired and inspected; 1990 is now verified as updated reprint. Named Joseph 16 December, second Trinity preface and Church-from-the-nations Mass still require exact Latin loci.
gaps.next_source: Original Latin 1981 and 2026 altar-book contents and named changed loci; separate 2008 calendar/lectionary, 2010 saints calendar/lectionary and 2015 Vigil book. Official 2024 frontmatter printed VI supplies exact promulgation dates and scope.
gaps.consequence: Second-recension structural changes have full-act evidence; no exact Latin wording, complete diff or extra reform for each publication/reprint is inferred.

gaps.missing: Original 1902 typical-edition images and the 1594 original. The 1954-to-1981 original comparison is now made for four units, and the 1475-to-1640 Veronica comparison is image-checked.
gaps.next_source: Institutional 1902 typical edition (Ward cites pp. 330 and 401-402) to test the 1954 censor's conformity certificate at those loci; 1594 BL Legg 137.
gaps.consequence: Text-collated transitions now exist for bounded units only; no checked transcription, comparison payload or inherited liturgical text is delivered.

gaps.period: Postconciliar reform, attested in the 1981 Latin book
gaps.missing: The Roman-Missal side of Ward's account: the 1970/1975 Roman prefaces from which, according to Ward, the reformed Passion-of-John preface (MA 384/6) was adapted and through which the old Sebastian preface wording reached the Common-of-Martyrs super populum (MA 483/2). The Ambrosian old and new texts are now compared original-to-original from 1954 to 1981 (ambrosian-1954-to-1981-prefaces); the 1902 side is tracked under ambrosian-gap-images.
gaps.next_source: Missale Romanum 1970 and 1975 typical editions: the preface of St John the Baptist and the first preface of martyrs, compared with 1981 MA 384/6 and MA 483/2; Ward, Notitiae 32 (1996), pp. 240–242 and 266–267 nn. 71–73 for his Roman loci.
gaps.consequence: The Roman-Missal route of these borrowings remains Ward's attribution; no reception or borrowing edge from the Roman Missal to the 1981 Ambrosian book is drawn from shared wording.
